entry.title: LizstarTrek - Starfleet Acadamy Season 1 episodes 5 - 10
entry.content:
Every Sunday my Twitch subs and I watch Star Trek in my Discord. Here are my reviews and thoughts on each of the episodes as I see it. If you’re curious about a nerd’s views on Star Trek episodes, please read on, I go quite in depth with some of these episodes! I’ve watched some Star Trek before but not all of it!

Finally done with Discovery, thank god. It’s time for the newest show of the whole lot, as of this writing, we’re almost FINALLY caught up. Despite this being directly after Discovery and tying into it in many ways, I’ve heard good things about it. So let’s be optimistic.

Though we did some research into pre-production and Kurtzman kept saying this was “the hip and cool Trek for the youths” and holy shit, dude, could you be any more Old Man?

Series Acclimation Mil - DIS 8.5/10

Holy shit we’re getting episodes about specific characters. That’s like, Old Trek shit. We’re allowed to do that?! This episode is about Series Acclimation Mil, also known as Sam. She starts the episode by just… talking to you while walking through the commons. It’s very interesting cause its directly from her point of view, and her point of view is pretty damn weird. She’s walking through, shaking everyone’s hands, and acting like the main character.

Basically, Sam was made by “the makers” who became sentient after being mistreated and used as slave labor by some species that died out ages ago. They want to open up and learn about others and be friends, but are also understandably hesitant, so Sam was went out to learn about Organics so she could explain them to them more easily.

A lot of the episode is actually first person as she talks to people directly to try and learn about them. As we are WELL AWARE by now, Sam is… blunt, and unable to fully comprehend when to not talk, so she’s just going up and asking Caleb “so you clearly want to have sex with her but do not, why is that?” I DO like Sam, but a lot of the humor with her is awkward humor, and that is 1000% not my jam.

Anyways, the plot of this episode is that the Makers want Sam to enroll in a specific class but when she approaches the teacher, she’s told “dude it’s midterms???” by this teacher, Illa. Illa is played by Mariner’s actress btw, who is ALSO the writer, and the first Trek star to become a writer for Trek. But Sam wants to prove she can handle it and takes on a big project about Benjamin Sisko. REMEMBER HIM?? We get a big ol’ lore update about Sisko and who he is. I know. It’s my favorite Trek :) But it does a good enough job reminding you. Anyways she’s like “oh, he was the Emissary. I’m an Emissary for my Makers! I must know what his deal is so I can become a good Emissary too”. Maybe don’t take Emissary lessons from Sisko.

She then offends every Bajoran in school by demanding they tell her if Sisko is alive or dead. Is… is this a metaphor for fans??

Our B plot is that Ake is trying to be nicer to Kelrec, who is currently… heating the pacific ocean so that an emissary from some planet he’s trying to get on good terms with is happy. She’s like “wtf you doing dog”

I’ve always said I wanted a sequel to DS9. This isn’t that, but it’s continuing a lot of it and honestly it has some similarities (both take place in a static space and are a little more slice of life-y). Here’s Jake! Nice to see him as grown up tbh. This is a hologram from the Sisko Museum, which notably also has a family tree on it that does NOT include Kassidy’s unborn kid at the end of DS9. Is this…. dark confirmation about a miscarriage? New horrifying lore dropped.

Things aren’t going well and the Makers are like “WE CREATED YOU WE CAN DECIDE WHAT TO DO WITH YOU AND IF YOU FAIL TO SHOW ANY OF THIS IS WORTH IT WE WILL LOCK YOU UP AND RETREAT FROM ORGANICS FOREVER”. So uh… doing what their creators did to THEM, I see. Anyways, she has one week left. She spends this time going to the bar with her friends, cause Sisko went there once. She doesn’t really know what she’s doing but frankly neither do we.

Sam gets smashed at the club, and declares “Oh I get it. Being an emissary means you never get to do whatever you want, ever. Sisko probably just wanted to eat shrimp and grits and build sailboats” and I mean, yeah. But after she starts a bar fight and gets in trouble, she goes back to the teacher who gives her a nudge and hands her Jake Sisko’s book. Sam then has a heart to heart in her mind with Jake, and then THIS drops

Dax is STILL AROUND. Half Cardassian Half Trill, btw.

She ends up being like “I’m not QUITTING and will hit you up when I can to give you updates but hey I’m my own person, bai bitches” and then cuts off her Makers. Fuck yea, fuck them.

We end with a Sisko voice over. It’s pretty nice. AND we end with the DS9 Theme!!! Hot damn.

Come, Let’s Away - DIS 8/10

This episode starts with an epileptic warning. Huh. Are you allowed to do anything you want if you warn people first? Time for red and blue flashing on every other frame!!

Caleb and Tarima fuck, and then have pillow talk about alien mating rituals, which is… fascinating.

That comes back fast though, as Betazoid’s sex involves like, connecting with the other person’s mind, and she sees a bunch of Caleb’s past involving his mom, which he reacts VERY poorly to. He’s offended by the idea that she got in his head without warning and permission but she’s a fucking telepath, dude. Maybe she’s not the right partner for you??? Anyways things are now VERY awkward.

The classes are assigned to a ship as a test exercise. Should be nice and simple with no major problems happening! They need to board a shut down ship and restore power. Caleb does it immediately cause he’s a smarty pants for engineering. Aaand as soon as he does a bunch of ships show up and “claim it as salvage”. They’re weird cannibal pirates called the “Furies”. They eat the lt cmdr who was teaching the kids on the ship, whoops!! It’s really cronchy and wet sounding!

The War College Klingon who’s been sassing them all season is like “A great man once said the needs of the many outweight the needs of the few, or the one” as a call to sacrifice himself. Hey, yeah, do you remember how is friends reacted to that? We got a whole fucking movie out of it.

They need someone with experience beating the Furies. And you know who’s beaten them before and knows their weaknesses? Paul Giamatti! I mean, Nus Braka. He’s absolutely fucking nuts, I love him. He quotes Sound of Music and says something tastes like cat piss. He’s a VERY interesting Klingon/Tellerite. He is 100% willing to work with them, IF they do him a favor. See, he was scamming people and had a toll road for who now can just use the dilithium that the Federation is giving them to go around him. He wants them to stop supplying Dilithium to these people. Kinda… fucked up and evil, but it IS a step below cannibalism, so we’re still on the even ground here! Also he’s got the hots for Ake and is a fucking creepy. Is… is thios going to suddenly veer into assault? God please do not.

Okay no, he’s just… kinda mocking her about how her son died in a situation very simialr to this. What’s your end goal, dude? Be an asshole?

Tarima has a condition that makes it so her psychic abilities are WAY stronger than they should be. She can connect with Caleb and gives him information and orders, which she does. As they talk psychically, he apologizes for being a fuckass during sex. Not 100% the time, but your head is in the right place.

Also Braka finally ponies up. The Furies’ weakness is they are part back, basically, and are very weak to sonic weapons. Those aren’t very common, so they order some from a nearby weapons facility. I feel if that thing is nearby they could have… sent a lot of other things to kill them all, but this works too. They’re gonna knock the Furies out, lower the shields, beam the kids out, and dip. …Except yeah, Braka double crossed them, they were working together the whole time. Giamatti just wanted to get a bit extra on the side I guess. ALSO his raiders attacked the station they called reinforcements from now that it was weakened and ransacked it. Wow, if you can’t trust the worst dude in space.

This does not go well. The Vulcan cadet is killed, Tarima rips her inhibitor so she can use her powers to help them, making psychic sonar weapons, basically. Just… Jean Grey-ing them to death, honestly.

Admiral Sexypants puts out a massive bounty on his head. “No one sleeps until we hunt him down and end him”. Yeah, I dunno wtf he was thinking, he’s now at war. Hopefully this will be worth it, dude. He actually sends a message directly to Ake, saying how much he fucking hates her, and the Federation, because they “think they’re better than him” and think he’s a “lowlife” for just living his life the way he wants to. Also he says he’s ready for them. I mean, your way of life is killing innocents to get yourself more things, so yeah. You are a lowlife :) It’s a good speech, he’s a fun villain.

Ko’Zeine - DIS 8/10

It’s been a bit since the last episode. Tarima lived, but basically had a brain version of a heart attack and is recovering at home. Caleb can’t send her a message, he’s in his own mind too much. Sam is injured. Yes, Sam. Her holomatrix is damaged and is slowly being repaired. And Genesis is now on the fast track for captaincy. Wowee.

omfg. Okay, so, the war college kids? There are four main ones. There’s Tarima. There’s the vulcan and his girl, the vulcan died. And then there’s Kyle. I haven’t mentioned Kyle, but Kyle’s deal is that the other war college kids are aggressive and kinda bullies and he’s like “Hi guys :)” and is just a nice friendly guy. He and Kraag have been hanging out more and chilling together and they are fucking they are SO fucking they are very VERY fucking. It’s honestly adorable. They’re going on a trip to Ibiza! Darem is jealous >:(

Everyone is packing up for the break and going home. omfg Ake packs her suitcase like I do. “YOU’RE TAKING FOUR PAIRS OF SHOES, AND YOU DON’T EVEN WEAR SHOES??” Anyways, Darem isn’t planning to go home but then people come and kidnap him, using portal tech, which is NOT common in Trek. Kraag runs in after him, and suddenly finds himself as best man in his wedding. Which is a thing that happens with Kionians. Poor Jay-Den is out of his element. Darem’s fiance is enby! Nice.

Genesis and Caleb both snuck back to campus because they don’t really have anywhere else to be, and just play stupid games they make up. Genesis is like “so how’s the girlfriend?” and Caleb is VERY bad at hiding he’s bad at this. They accidentally let a Warp Slug out, and we get a big humorous scene with Reno having a conversation with her wife. Also they kill the poor slug ): Poor baby

Darem really needs his bro Jay-Den there, because he’s struggling with this. The wedding wasn’t going to be for a while, but they had to call it early cause he’s marrying the princess and she needs to be queen NOW cause her parents are abdicating early to retire. He’s basically giving up his entire life and personal goals out of duty and responsibility, and he will do it without whining, but he wants his bro there to help. It’s a bit sad.

….okay, there is 100% something going on with Darem and Jay-Den. This is the gayest Trek, and all of it has actually been handled really well.

Neli made a good point in how this episode is the inverse of the traditional “take part in this Klingon ceremony even if it makes everything really awkward”. I’d no joke love an episode where like, Worf had to go to a Bar Mitzvah and make an ass of himself.

Genesis uses Caleb to sneak onto the ship and steal some stuff so she can get access to her records to change things because without it, she’ll be expelled, apparently. But we don’t find out what that means cause Reno finds them and they are in the DEEPEST of shit.

Kraag storms off to find a way home but ends up deliverying the best man speech anyway. This speech rips the new queen apart. Because the person he was describing is someone she never met. And she realizes if he does this it’s just to appease her and everyone else. So she asks him to abdicate and annuls the marriage.

Genesis and Caleb just get menial labor, and Genesis is taken off of pre-command track. We also find out menial labor is literally just cleaning stuff. Genesis finally talks Caleb into not being an idiot and he messages his girlfriend.

The Life of the Stars - DIS 10/10

Tarima is back at the acadamy. She’s being transfered to Starfleet, instead of the War College. She’s not handling the people hovering around her too well. She’s… struggling, obviously. She’s been pushed out of the war college because her condition will put her in danger if she gets more physical, so she only really has a future in non-war stuff.

The cadets are struggling to get together, and are not handling the trauma well. So they send in the big guns.

Tilly is their teacher for… THEATER CLASS. Yes, Tilly is FINALLY HERE! I thought this show would be MADE FOR HER, but instead she’s here for a single episode as a guest star. wtf. Anyways no one is happy about this… except Sam, who is super excited.

This basically has four plots, all very important. Plot A) They are all doing theater and researching plays, they’re gonna do Our Town. Tarima is assigned Emily. B) Caleb and Tarima are on the outs because Tarima is handling this so poorly. Caleb is awkward and doesn’t know how to handle it. C) Sam is malfunctioning from being injured two episode ago and they’re gonna go to her home planet to try and fix her. D) Jay-Den has a cold! :)

Tarima gets fucking wasted and finally reaches out out to Caleb. She’s fucking druuuunk and finally comes back onto Caleb, but he’s like “wait no, you’re drunk, we should not” and she does noooot handle it well. “Oh you’re afraid of being with the head melty girl? Afraid of fucking the monster?” No girl you’re drunk. You can melt my head when you’re sober though, hit me up. There’s also stuff here about how obviously Caleb and Genesis are into each other, too. I was feeling hints of that last episode.

The way this episode handles the PTSD and fear of it all is actually pretty good. It’s kind of a modern take on Only A Paper Moon. Maybe not as good, but still good. She has a breakdown in class about it and finally opens up to everyone.

The Kasque do a thing that’s… kind of like the Great Link but for holograms? They “overwhelm” her and search through her data to see what’s wrong with her. It’s pretty creepy. They determine she is broken beyond repair. “What took us two hundred years to build you destroyed in 209 days.” Damn.

We get a few really good scenes about this. Her friends are worried for her and act out the play Sam loved. Meanwhile, the Doctor explains why this is so tough on him. We get references to the episode where he made a hologram family. Holy SHIT I’m surprised we’re calling back to that. We also learn the reason she’s failing is actually NOT cause of the damage she took, but cause she wasn’t built to properly process trauma and grief so it’s cascading. They need to reprogram her with a childhood so she can properly handle the trauma, and the Doctor can be the parent! He is NOT happy about this. As he says too, he is a coward. But he finally agrees. Due to the way time works on Kasque, it’ll only be a few days, but feel like 17 years for the Doctor and Sam.

We get scenes of them living together as daughter and father, with voice over from Occam from the play. It’s… quite good!

Tilly gets a send off as Tarima basically thanks her for helping her move on. The episode ends with Ake basically as the Stage Manager from the play but for this show.

I feel like if I had read the play this would have been even better. It’s kinda on the cusp of a 9.5 and a 10 but I’ll be nice. This is prolly the last 10 Trek is ever getting anyway. Gotta be kind. I do prefer Paper Moon but y’know, I also had watched 7 seasons of Rom. I bet if this was season 7 this woulda kicked my ass even more.

300th Night - DIS 7.5/10

Its the end of the semester! Everyone is partying! And they’re doing the Brother Bonding ritual in Kraag’s room, which is neat. Remember when Worf did that? Fun callback. Everyone is bonded now… except Caleb, who pusses out and runs out and has an awkward conversation with his on again off again on the holodeck. Calebs not having a fun party day.

Meanwhile we learn what it is Paul Giamatti stole. Some Omega particles. Specifically “Omega 147”, a stable variant of Omega. That one’s from Voyager! More Clap Nerds moments, but hey, I don’t usually mind it that much.

Sam is back and okay btw, though she’s a bit different. She’s embarassed by how she used to act. “You were one year old, it’s understandable”. She also helps Caleb figure out something he’s been missing about his mother, and he tries to find her messages again with some new outlook aaaand instantly finds two years of them. Ey, this storyline might be reaching its conclusion! They listen to the most recent one and find out that Paul Giamatti is invading where she appears to be right now.

He goes looking for help, but everyone’s is pretty on edge about all of this. They can’t really send any Starfleet ships to help, cause they need to protect Betazed to keep the Federation stable. He then says some weird cryptic shit to Tarima that would immediately make me go “I’m calling medical”.

Sam and Caleb are stealing a shuttle. Well, Caleb doesn’t want Sam to help, but Sam wants to help. Darem stumbles in drunk as fuck, and Genesis is basically kidnapped and brought along for the ride. Leaving poor Jay-Den out of the climax ): Jay-Den’s job is to basically tell Tarima what’s going on so SHE can go to the adults and get the Athena to chase after their asses. (Apparently Jay-Den’s actor was having issues with prosthetics, so prolly why he’s kinda written out, a real shame) Ake goes to Admiral Daddy and is like “Hey you promised me you’d help me keep Caleb safe” and he goes “ah shit. Well if you chase them to enemy territory, I cannot help you”. Damn. STILL a good admiral.

Caleb finds his mom! At knife point, but then it turns into a crying hug. Aww.

LOL “Captain, we found some possibilities of some people sneaking around on board!” Aaaand it’s Kraag and Tarima. “H-how?” “If you increase pressure by 0.29% in a room it blocks life signs.” “THAT… IS A DESIGN FLAW.” lmfao. And honestly a kind of realistic design flaw, I’d bet something like that is real. They were just trying to sneak out to save their friends. Oh those crazy kids.

Caleb tells his friends they all gotta go their seperate ways. No one is happy about this. To try and get them to go away without any kind of regrets, he tries to tear them down. It doesn’t really work. They know how he is. He’s just a “messed up little kid”. But then when they’re all captured by Venari Ral, Caleb has to save them. He also sends a message to Ake telling them where they are.

A shootout happens. The Venari Ral are… I dunno how they feel as villains. They’re like…. I dunno what they’re supposed to be. But they’re very mustache twirlingly evil and will just kill federation citizens if they even think someone might be federation, all while cackling about it. Why? I dunno. Cause they’re evil. Ake comes in to save all of them, though Caleb’s mom is injured in the process.

The Venari Ral are using Isolytic weapons?? WHY DO THEY HAVE THAT?!

The Venari Ral have set up a ring of mines around the entirety of Federation space. Hey, remember when we set up mines around a SINGLE wormhole and it was super dangerous and hard to set up and we needed a fucking genius to do it? They must have a Rom on their payroll.

Ohhh Caleb’s mom is NOT happy she’s under Federation custody.

Rubincon - DIS 9/10

Shit is bad. They can’t get back to Fedspace, and are under attack as Braka comes to bear. And then this dude fucking teleports onto Ake’s ship DIRECTLY ONTO HER CAPTAIN’S CHAIR. He legit said to his transport officer” put me on her chair, I wanna piss her off even more”. What an asshole, I love that.

Braka says he doesn’t like Reno. That’s how you know he’s a bad guy!

They hide the cadets from scans by doing the 0.29% pressure thing.

Braka takes Ake, Caleb’s mom, and then blows the fuck out of the ship. RIP everyone. No okay, they did a big hologram maneuver to make it SEEM like they asplode. Okay so now it’s all the kids… and captain Reno. This is what we’ve literally all wanted since season 2 of Discovery. She’s very Reno around all of this.

Ake and Ashisha (Caleb’s mom) now have to work together, as Ake sneaks her hints that Caleb is alive. They’re there as Braka gives an announcement.

I’M HAVING AN ANNOUNCEMENT

THE FEDERATION IS A BITCHASS MOTHERFUCKER. IT PISSED ON MY FUCKING WIFE.

No he’s actually doing a big-ass Nolan Batman style speech and scene where he’s putting the Federation “on trial”. Q he ain’t.

Okay. I’m going to make a declaration. For the end of this season and into next season, of what I want. I want Ake and Anisha to start dating. Hear me out, okay? It’ll work. IT’LL WORK.

ALSO IT’LL MAKE EVERYONE ANGRY AS FUCK, WHAT ELSE COULD WE WANT

As Anisha tears into her, Ake looks a fuckin’ wreck. “I HOPE YOU THINK ABOUT ME EVERY DAY, ABOUT WHAT YOU DID.” Um. She already does.

The Doctor is broken and his language processor is broken. He’s trying to tell them things, but they can’t understand him. Sam is also still mad at Genesis for how she THINKS Genesis treated her before she became more… adult. But they finally have a heart to heart, and using that Sam works out what the Doctor is trying to say. They need to use… Rubin Particles or whatever to try and stop the Omega Mines. They find a way to do it, but need to take on Braka directly, basically.

To guide them there, they’re gonna use Tarima’s psychic powers. She’s been told all her life she can’t control these powers, but Caleb gives her a pep talk and she’s willing to try again.

It works! She also confesses her love. Cute!

They make it there just as Caleb’s mom declares Ake guilty. Caleb reacts to this by… taking a shuttle down to make his declaration to the quadrant on TV. And his declaration is that Acadamy helped saved him. He ALSO helps tear down a lie Braka made. Braka said his home, a Strontium mining colony, exploded in red Federation weapon fire cause fuck them, the Federation is evil and wanted them dead for no reason. Well no, obviously. Strontium explodes red when used as weapons, improperly. He was just told as a little kid that to make sense of it. And he’s still living as that little kid, unlike Caleb, who was but grew up over the season.

It’s a good theme. I DO wish they had built this up over the season tbh, it feels like they just shoved this into his character at the end. I liked Braka, he was fun, I liked watching him, but he was pretty one note.

Anyways everyone abandons Braka over this, and he throws a tantrum and decides to blow up the mine field… which has now been shut down. The Federation shows up, arrests Braka. Anisha punches him. “YOU CALL THAT A PUNCH?” Ake punches him, and he can’t help but go “OOUUGGHHHH”

OH MY GOD. ANISHA AND AKE ARE FLIRTING. HOLY SHIT.

I FUCKING CALLED IT.

MY YURI SENSES HAVE NEVER BEEN FINER TUNED.

Caleb is going to stay with his mom during Summer, but this is his home, and he will be coming back. But now he has two homes. It ends with him spending time with his friends as Reno and her wife walk by holding hands.

This was a good season!!!

entry.content:
Every Sunday my Twitch subs and I watch Star Trek in my Discord. Here are my reviews and thoughts on each of the episodes as I see it. If you’re curious about a nerd’s views on Star Trek episodes, please read on, I go quite in depth with some of these episodes! I’ve watched some Star Trek before but not all of it!

So I LOVED seasons 1 and 2 of SNW. But I…. did not really enjoy season 3. And as we were sitting here trying to remember what happened, we kind of couldn’t. So… maybe this will be better!!!

Valles Marineris - SNW 5.5/10

Everyone is horse riding on a planet and having a good time. Yay, horses! Everything is nice and happy after last season’s horrifying nonsense! When Pike gets back he’s told “we want to promote you to admiral. Let us know after your next mission what your answer is”. He doesn’t seem very happy about the idea. Meanwhile, Uhura has a new cadet that she gets to show around the ship and mentor! She’s a Vulcan who’s abrasive, rude, and an asshole. Oh. Good. More poorly written Vulcans.

The mission is to go check out a storm, and when they get there they get an SOS from someone inside the storm. The ship reacts in the storm by… spinning the camera around in circles. Hooooly shit that made me very motion sick. The storm knocks out, and they’re dead in the water in the middle of a weird warp field at the center of the storm.

They go to a nearby planet to get materials to reignite their warp core. They land on a weird planet that has giant animals. While they’re down there, something grabs the ship and drags them away. …did we go back to prehistoric Earth? Are these the Saurians? Oh PLEASE let it be the Voth!

The aliens are like “We are taking your damaged ship as salvage :)” Pike invites their commander… onto the ship to “show her weapons”, which isn’t ideal. They ALSO learn where they are! In the Sol system. 65 million years ago. Yes! YES! VOTH!!! There are three M class planets here for some reason, interesting.

Oh. Those aren’t Voth ):

Darn. These are the Martians. They’re super… militaristic. And they ONLY care about weapons and killing their enemy, the Dol’drm, and nothing else. Even when just talking about CARROTS, she goes “is this a weapon?” Girl. Not everything has to be about killing people.

They actually make some progress, this seems to go well, they try and help the Martians make peace with the Dol’drm… and then the Martians just start stealing shit. The head Martian lady has found out they’re from the future, the Federation doesn’t really exist, and therefore an alliance with them means nothing so they’re just going to steal their shit and leave.

Back on Earth, we’ve GOT A RAPTOR PUPPET! It’s basically Yoshi from the Mario movie. La’an punches it in the snoot. Poor raptor ): We ALSO find out from this.. La’an breaks her hand, feels no pain, and they determine her augment DNA has activated. She doesn’t THINK she’s going to try and kill everyone and take over the galaxy! But hey, we’ve had bad experiences with augments in the past.

The Martians are headed to the Dol’drm’s planet, a 5th planet in the Solar System, between Mars and Jupiter. Enterprise moves to stop the explosion, but… Pike refuses to order the bomb destroyed. Yeah, this is a self fulfilling time loop, and they need to let that planet explode, become the asteroid belt, and then use the blast wave to travel to the future. Which they do. This explosion ALSO sends the asteroid to Earth, hitting it and extincting dinosaurs.

They go real into why they had to do what they do, or had to NOT do what they wanted to do. Yes. I know how a self fulfilling time loop works. This is not a show for 4 year olds.

They also learn that the Martians may have gone extinct because of what happened (Mar’s orbit got changed nad cooled) but they did manage to escape and spread their DNA around the galaxy, though by now there’s no real group of them anymore. The uh, the Dol’drm was prolly not as lucky. But they had to die so that they could exist. “I’d have done the same thing the Martians did,” said Pike. What? No. They weren’t able to communicate and didn’t even try. You would NOT have done what they did, you would have at least TRIED for a peaceful solution.

Anyways they’re back home. Pike of course shoots down the promotion and gives it to Una, who is now Commander U- WHAT. COMMANDER? SHE WASN’T A COMMANDER ALREADY?!?!?! WHAT THE FUCK?! Also the Vulcan continues to be a piece of shit and says she’s gonna leave. AND they’re pushing Ortegas into Scotty. Ohhh no. They’re gonna hetero Ortegas up ):

The Griffin Incident - SNW 3/10

Kirk, Spock, and La’an are responding to a weird SOS signal they found. It’s an old SOS signal, and they find a ship called the Griffin, a ship that went missing 9 years ago.

They beam on board and Kirk starts hearing a baby crying while the others do not. Ohhh we’re doin’ some ghost ship stuff. Maybe even some Magnetic Rose shit! Neat.

Yep. Time for horror.

They all see a ghost to disappears. They also find a door that’s been sealed shut, telling them some things. 1) They were not the first person to board this ship. 2) Those earlier people were Federation, Klingon, and Vulcan. 3) They sealed the door AND tried to open it.

They find out what happened, kind of. They find out who the ghost they saw was, a member of the Griffin’s crew, who was reporting the crew was acting erratically. She was confined to quarters, and became convinced they were all under control of some alien force and she was the only one left. So she just… killed them. Strangling some, spacing others. This crew member supposedly removed their bodies and moved them… somewhere.

Things start happening randomly. Body bags that were empty fill with bloody corpses. One gets up and moves behind Spock. The crewmember’s log starts SPEAKING to La’an, and the one moving behind Spock also speaks to him. Also they shuttle randomly died. Uh oh, they’re stuck on this weird-ass ship.

The moving body was T’Pring!! She’s like “what why am I here” and Spock is like “Yeah I’d like to know that too”. Spock’s current theory is there’s a psychotropic effect causing him to hallucinate. He even starts bugging out in a Vulcan way.

All three are buggin’ out in different ways. La’an sees the murderer, Rose Harper, who’s trying to get her to kill people like she did. Kirk hears and sees his son David crying. Tie in to Search for Spock! Spock sees his ex, who ends up taking his gun and shooting him, then… cuts his ears off. That’s… horrifying.

The rest of the crew show up and rescue Kirk, who is clearly unstable and shakey.

This episode is clearly trying to be the horror episode. Lots of not knowing whats real and whats not, lots of weird unsettling things. Lots of things not workign the way it’s supposed to work. I don’t hate it by any means, but I dunno if it works. I can’t relaly explain why though.

La’an and Spock are rescued, Spock with his ears snipped off. La’an, Uhura, and Erica try to beam off, but La’an nearly kills Erica in a teleporter, and Una and Pike start trying him down again, Una cutting into herself. Jesus, this episode. Sam starts monologuing to Kirk. Obviously none of these people are actually real, it’s weird as hell. Sam gets slammed against a window and we see his INTESTINES GET SUCKED OUT OF HIM THROUGH THE WINDOW.

WHAT IS THIS EPISODE? WHY IS THIS SO GRAPHIC?!

La’an finally fully loses her self to insanity. She ends up stabbing Kirk… maybe for real?

PIKE IS CHOPPING HIS FINGERS OFF. WHAT IS THIS EPISODE?!?!?!

Anyways Spock manages to force his way out of the hallucinations, making it clear he was cutting his own ears off. They’re all teleported off the ship, and they quickly take Jim off to medbay to try and help him. …Or they just stare at him and talk instead. wtf are y’all doing? Teleport that man now?!?! Also when they beamed back to the Enterprise, La’an with a knife about to stab Jim again, they’re all standing there staring, mouth agape. That’s what we all look like watching this episode.

We get scenes of people talking to the survivors. Chapel talks to Spock, Pike talks to La’an, and Uhura talks to Kirk, all trying to help them recooperate and come to terms with what they saw. Kirk then calls his kid. These are… good scenes, but man, this episode really took me out of it.

I don’t think it’s a…. BAD idea. But it could have like, really been good character development and it felt like it was trying but it didn’t really hit. And then it was just shock horror. We watched Hellraiser and The Thing this holloween, and THIS is what upset Neli (she does not like horror or violence)

entry.title: Retro Achievement Mastery 238 - Art of Balance

link.title: Retro Achievement Mastery 238 - Art of Balance

entry.content:
Last time I said most of the Wii stuff I mastered during the rollout was shovelware. I was expecting this to be one of those. It is not.

I played Wiiware already, with La-Mulana, but let’s talk about it specifically. Wiiware was the name for downloadable games off the Wii shop channel, with its sick-ass tunes, and were almost never sold directly in stores. It was like the Xbox Live Arcade for Wii stuff. And much like Xbox360 and PS3 VS the Wii for regularly released games, a lot of it is shovelware motion slop. Just shit for grandma or little kids that uses a waggle motion… right?

No, not at all. This is Art of Balance, and it really surprised me.

Art of Balance is very, very simple. You have a little zen bowl of water, and a bunch of blocks. You need to balance those blocks in such a way that it doesn’t ripple the water. Usually the way the water ripples is shit falling into it, but dipping stuff in is off limits, too. And… that’s it! There are four worlds. 124 levels in total, I think. Just balance stuff.

There is a LITTLE more than that. There are glass pieces which can break if you put too many pieces on them, as well as pieces that will break if you put ANYTHING on them after enough time has passed. Sometimes you WANT things to break, and can plan accordingly.

There’s no one answers for any of these puzzles. It’s a physics puzzle, and physics in videogames are fucked up and wonky, always. So you can find some truly diabolical ways to get through these levels.

I actually had a blast playing this game. It probably cost, what, 15 dollars on release? Easily worth it. It uses the motion controls for precise careful placement, has a chill atmosphere, and is really rewarding to finally beat that messed up level you’ve been stuck on. I can see why this is a bit of a cult classic for Wiiware.

entry.title: LizstarTrek - Starfleet Acadamy Season 1 episodes 1 - 4
entry.content:
Every Sunday my Twitch subs and I watch Star Trek in my Discord. Here are my reviews and thoughts on each of the episodes as I see it. If you’re curious about a nerd’s views on Star Trek episodes, please read on, I go quite in depth with some of these episodes! I’ve watched some Star Trek before but not all of it!

Finally done with Discovery, thank god. It’s time for the newest show of the whole lot, as of this writing, we’re almost FINALLY caught up. Despite this being directly after Discovery and tying into it in many ways, I’ve heard good things about it. So let’s be optimistic.

Though we did some research into pre-production and Kurtzman kept saying this was “the hip and cool Trek for the youths” and holy shit, dude, could you be any more Old Man?

Kids These Days - DIS 7.5/10

We’re introduced to a small kid, Caleb Mir, who’s in a waiting cell with his Mom, who’s saying a whole lot of things that are saying “I am not going to be here for long”. She also gives him a weird creepy toy.

Apparently the two of them were working with a pirate, named Paul Giamatti. Wait shit, I’m sorry, his name is Paul Giamatti. Fuck, I mean- Anyways, Paul Giamatti really REALLY wanted to play a Klingon villain, and you can tell, he’s having the time of his life. He’s sent to prison, and Caleb’s mom is sent too for being an accomplice. Caleb then plays them for fools with the “I’m a little innocent kid~” shtick and breaks out of jail. This guy is gonna be our prococious scamp for the series who will have to learn the true meaning of friendship.

We then jump 15 years later. He’s a prisoner again. Damn, dude, can’t catch a break huh? He breaks free then is captured again. Maybe quit while you’re ahead.

We meet this lady, Nahla Ake, a half Human half Lanthanite. She was the captain who split up Caleb and his mom and lost him 15 years ago. She resigned over it cause she’s like “what I was told to do what fucked up and I refuse to have anything to do with it.” Admiral Sexypants from Discovery is like “hey we know where he is, maybe come out of retirement”. So she does, she goes to pick Caleb up and gets him to sign a deal saying “do community service with me at Starfleet Acadamy, and I help you find your mom, who btw broke out of jail a year ago and hasn’t even tried looking for you? That’s fucked up”

PRetty good character motivations so far. Discovery also started with a criminal who has to be forced into servitude to help the Federation, but uh, Caleb is a kid? He’s not an XO who makes dumb angry decisions for no reason. He’s a KID who makes dumb decisons for no reason! I can get behind that way better.

We get lots of shotgunning jokes and scenes introducing the rest of the cast. Lura Thok, a Jem Hadar/Klingon hybrid who’s a hardcore “YES SIR, STAND UP SOLDIER” type. “LET ME SEE YOUR WAR FACE!” Jay-Den, a Klingon cadet who’s signed up for medical stuff because he wants to “live a valiant life”. He also apologizes, which is a weird thing for a Klingon. I think I like his vibe already. Then of course, ya boi, the Doctor. I’m just happy to see him tbh. Also this Starfleet acadamy class takes place in a space ship that looks like the fucking Halo laser sword, and Ake sits in her chair in the most bisexual way I have ever seen.

Also, that’s three hybrid characters so far I think?? Ake, Thok, and and Paul Giamatti are all hybrid peoples. That’s rad tbh. More of that, please. This shit is a melting pot, let that pot MELT. No wonder this series pissed off fascists.

We get a scene of some rich kid bullying the Klingon for some fucking reason while everyone is like “WHAT ARE YOU DOING WHY ARE YOU DOING THAT” but only Caleb actually stands up for him and gets him his binoculars back. Jay-Den likes to go bird watching. I legit love this guy already??? He’s basically a Klingon I would write.

We also meet two other kids. Genesis, a kind of haughty but friendly girl, and SAM, a hologram. Or, as she prefers, “photonic”. Ohhh, Genesis is actually kind of a FREAK. “I want to learn how to kill a man with a toothbrush”. Caleb legit reacts by going “What the FUCK?” They’re also ALREADY teasing a romance between these two. That was fast.

The ship flies into a place that immediately tries to blow it up. Why the fuck are we doing that??? This ship has kids on it. What is it, the Enterprise? A big spiky obviously evil ship is blowing them the fuck up. The cadets all gotta step up once Lura gets stabbed by some debris. Caleb knows a way to stop this, and starts to work with it. We also learn who the villain here is. It’s Nus Braka, AKA Paul Giamatti! He’s fun. Apparently Giamatti’s favorite Trek is DS9 and you can tell cause he wants to be Gul Dukat. But like, a little less of a “convinces himself he’s the good guy” and leaning a bit more into the “Gul Dukat was a weird creepy pervert”. We also learn the reason he knows they’re here is cause Caleb is trying to send messages to his mom. Everyone blames him but like, I dunno dog, he was just trying to send messages to his mom.

All of the cadets get time to shine here. Even the rich pretty boy, Darem, shines. He’s “Khaonian”, which allows him to um… Mystique himself and live in space. He’s blue now, that’s his attack. Oh they’re also pushing stuff with him and Genesis. Time for a loooove trongle! Anyways Darem then almost freezes to death. I mean, that’s not how heat works in space, he wouldn’t radiate all that that fast, but that’s okay. Genesis ends up saving him using a tractor beam.

There’s actually some really good jokes here. A lot of them from Thok. “IF I AM GOING TO DIE TODAY, I NEED LESS CHEERFULNESS”. And when she gives a friendly shoulder punch to Jay-Den, he just goes flyyyiiiing. Also I like Caleb’s sass.

Caleb manages to do his thing and they blow up Giamatti’s ship. He escapes in an escape pod, laughing maniacally as he does.

We then get a weird slowmo flyby of each of the characters as a weird slow version of “If You’re Going To San Fransisco” plays. I’ve never been a huge fan of this kinda thing.

Captain Ake gives Caleb the chance to just… dip. He stays with them for 90 days and 100 hours of labor to pay off his jail time, and she helps him find his mom. OR he just leaves. He of course decides to stay, because she show has to happen.

I actually liked that. Honestly pretty up there for a first episode for a Trek series.

Beta Test - DIS 7.5/10

Everyone makes it to Starfleet Acadamy, the first class on campus in like 100 years cause y’know, Burn shenanigans. Also we get the intro for the first time. It looks like a cutscene from Civilization 4 that should have “Baba Yetu” playing over it.

Caleb and the pretty boy are roommates. Neither are happy about this.

EXOCOMP!!! There’s also a Brikar, Rak-Tahk’s species, that’s sick as hell.

This was the only thing I knew about this character. That she goes barefoot. Also that she sits in a bisexual manner. Anyways she’s talking with Admiral Sexpot and some other Federation bigwig who is immediatley unlikable. They’re trying to get Betazoid to rejoin the Federation. JETT RENO IS HERE!! I STILL LOVE HER. This is actually the most dialogue they ever gave her like… ever. She always showed up like every three episodes in Discovery to say two lines that were the best lines of the episode.

Apparently BDG was in this episode. He voiced a DOT that says “hello”. Jeremy Coulhain was the other one. That’s fucking wild. Also the school chime is the Trek theme, which means the Trek theme exists in the world of Trek. Who wrote the in universe Trek theme?

Caleb makes an ass out of himself in front of the princess of Betazed, basically. She teases the hell out of him in a “I am clearly into you but I’mma play with your emotions cause I know what they are~” kinda way. It’s a little cute, ngl. She tells the people in charge she wants him to be her guide around the campus. Everyone is like “HIM??????”

They connect in a nice way. He’s an awkward guy who can’t trust anyone due to his shitty-ass life. They go to Cetacean Ops for a date. Are they allowed to do that??? That’s Yuri appropriation. Also this is the first time we see Cetacean Ops in live action!!! Things kinda go south when the other Betazeds can’t contact her in Cetacean Ops, and they get in trouble. Well, Caleb gets in trouble. HE WAS DOING WHAT SHE WANTED?? SHE ASKED FOR IT? Also she gives him government secrets, showing her that the planet his mother is apparently on is behind the Betazed Psychic Wall.

Oh also I may have to mention, the Betazed leader speaks in sign language. I can’t believe Star Trek is woke now. Hey anyways I was thinking about one of my favorite TNG season 2 episodes recently, Loud As a Whisper, which had a mute actor as one of the main characters?

Anyways, the princess finds out Caleb is kinda using her to find his mom and won’t open up to her about why, and reacts poorly. The Betazed leader walks out of the negatiations partly because of this. And then we get a THIRD SCENE of Ake trying to convince Caleb not to leave. Hopefully this isn’t a thing that happens every episode.

Caleb opens up to the princess, being honest to someone else for once maybe since he was like, 4. He explains WHY he used her, and tries to convince her to help this move along. She does, and Betazed rejoins.

The princess joins… the War College. lol. But hey, her brother is now Caleb’s new roommate! He’s very awkward.

I do like all these episode so far, I think my #1 problem is they’re too long. Every episode is like an hour and 15 minutes.

Vitus Reflux - DIS 7.5/10

We get some stuff about the War College VS Starfleet. The War College cadets are…. weird assholes? And they start pranking the Starfleet Cadets for no reason. They hack the teleporters to drag them out of the locker room and into random spots on campus. And then brag about it over intercoms going “We do this cause we can. And cause it’s fun”. Um, expel them??

Also, Darem is bisexual and polyamarous. Holy shit. Are we going to get a polyam love triangle????

Thok tries to convince Ake to just… use authority to stop this. But she’s like “this is kid shit, and I’m for kid shit”. lol she’s a weirdo. She basically helps them get even, with some botony thing.

Meanwhile, Genesis signs Caleb up for a sports thing. He has NO interest, but she’s an admiral’s daughter and HAS to be leader, and has to win. To an unhealthy degree. And he’s the most obviously competent one there, except for maybe Jay-Den.

The sport is just laser tag! If Laser Tag was the Battle at Normandy. It’s so fucking funny the idea that they replaced Parrises Squares with a full phaser battle charge because it’s safer than Parrises Squares ever was. That’s so funny.

All of the characters are having moments where they talk and sass each other and oh my GOD imagine characters like, just having character moments and interracting in normal regular moments. Then you can have things stand out better when shit hits the fan! Instead of just like… having them only ever talk to each other when serious shit is going down.

Caleb talks to the Betazed Princess, who’s name is actually Tarima, I guess I need to name her since she’s around more often. She seems pretty distant about all of this. Who knows where this is going tbh

Darem wins captaincy of the sports team because he got Genesis mad my mocking her. Rude. At least he gets his comeuppance by having the war college people prank him again, but honestly it’s mostly aimed at them mocking poor Sam. Darem decides they’re going to do a sports match after hours to get back at them. They are very much outmatched and not gonna win. Genesis steps out of this because A) “A true captain doesn’t send their team into a slaughter” and B) “They don’t do underhanded shit like you did to win”. She’s 100% right. But then she shows up anyway cause I mean this guy is totally gonna whiz it down his leg.

Darem does in fact continually suck ass and his stretegies keep fucking them over. Genesis actually comes up with ideas and strategies and uses her training to win. Darem ends up quitting over this, but the game is ended anyways when the teachers find out about it and break it up. Everyone gets in massive trouble. Except Darem I guess. They react to this by uh…. trying to prank the war college even harder.

HOLY SHIT JETT RENO AND THOK ARE DATING?! Also Reno is 100% the top.

Darem says his mommy and daddy issues are the reasons he’s an asshole. They forgive him, but hope that he can be better.

The rest of the episode is a heist. Well, until this happens

Tarima aplogizes for being weird, buuuuut they’re still not super on the same terms. But she DOES kiss him! Oh, kids.

Anyways the prank goes without a hitch. And what ws the prank? Exactly the shit Ake had planned up and th ought of, cause she’s a pranking genius, and she kept feeding it to them through Code. That’s fun.

I liked this one too, but it was leaning a bit into the fratboy college stuff in a way that didn’t resonate with me, but it’s not BAD, just not super my thing. I do like when it all comes back to “Starfleet is good and all about empathy and working together for a better tomorrow” and that’s the main takeaway though.

Vox In Excelso - DIS 6.5/10

The Doctor is teaching debate. Jay-Den is NOT happy about this, he does not like public speaking. They do like, a tournament of debate. Caleb wins every single debate, hardcore. He’s actually very good at debate. When it gets to Jay-Den, he just… has a panic attack. Poor Jay-Den.

I REALLY like Caleb and Jay-Den’s friendship.

We also learn some Klingon lore. There were basically no Klingons in Discovery post time skip, so we learn a few things. The Burn caused Qo’noS to become uninhabitable and now Klingons are nearing extinction. That’s… that’s fucking nuts. What the fuck? They’re showing this off through a flashback montage. What the fuck is it with Modern Star Trek and blowing up the capital planets of the other major forces? This is the first major worldbuilding mistep of all of this. And y’all KNOW how I love my Klingons, so…

Anyways we learn that Jay-Den’s family might have died. And we get some flashbacks to him on a refugee planet. He was close with his brother, who supported him in what he wanted to do, but his dad didn’t understand and wanted him to be a warrior like the rest of them. But his brother is cool as hell. “Your mind is hungry, brother. We must feed it!” He wants to get his bro some Federation tech.

We’ve got two major plots. One, the debate team is basically debating the rights of the Klingons to… exist? And that they should be helped to survive? Not sure what’s going on there. Notably, Jay-Den is anti-Federation help. And Ake is going to try and talk to some Klingon leaders to offer them aid and help.

More flashbacks. Jay-Den’s brother is killed trying to trade for Federation technology. Jay-Den is not allowed to try and save him because of his parents’ bigotry.

Ake meets up with an old… “friend”. They were ABSOLUTELY fucking. They get smmmaaaashed. Okay yes, later on in a later scene, they were 100% fucking and it almost went somewhere but they were both too married to their jobs and cultures. A shame. They’re cute together.

Of ALL the people to help psych up and therapy Jay-Den, it’s Darem. Also it’s very, VERY gay.

It’s now the day of the debate. Ake is hung over. It doesn’t go well. Caleb VS Jay-Den ends with them yelling at each other Thok is like “Well I’ve never been an advisor for another Klingon and I don’t wanna fuck it up but I’ll do my best.” She rights his views on his family and is like “They didn’t abandon you, they let you go so you can be here in the only way they could”. It’s pretty nice.

Jay-Den goes back up to the debate stage so he can give a big debate about why the Federation shouldn’t just give the Klingons what they need, and force them to stop being Klingons. It’s a good scene, though I dunno why they have so many bright lights in my face. He ends up giving a new idea. “We should solve a Klingon problem with a Klingon solution.”

What’s that solution? Go to war with the Klingons. It’s all one big excuse to let the Klingons win the planet as spoils of war. Also frankly it’s foreplay for Ake and her klingon boytoy.

The episode is good. I do not like the stupid lore stuff with the Klingons but the writing and how they handled it in this episode were good. I just… man I wish we didn’t have to deal with the Burn still, and all the nonsense that came with it.

We cut it to four episodes tonight cause holy SHIT why are these episodes an hour and 20 minutes?????

Whistlespeak - DIS 3/10

This looks like a 1999 point and click adventure game background

“Maybe try scanning every culture in the database for ones that put an emphasis on the importance of water” YOU MEAN ALL OF THEM?

Tilly and Michael beam down because Michael will be cold in the fucking grave before anyone does anything without her.

It’s a dangerous run though, I like non-offensive native cultures. Also Michael drops out of the race, so it’s up to Tilly to possibly win, which means maybe Tilly will get to do a thing!

Hot man alert. Say the line, Liz.

Tilly ends up befriending one of the other racers and helps her to cross the finish line. It’s cute, and a good moment. Aaaand then it turns out those who win the race will be killed to help “bring the rain” and “meet the gods”. Oh boy.

Meanwhile, back on Discovery, Adira is having a lot of anxiety cause they’re put on the bridge on an important mission and y’know, that shit’s scary. Poor Adira.

Tilly and her friend are locked in a big stone tower. Discovery can’t get a lock on them. Dude. Anyways Michael breaks the prime directive to get them to open the door. Just fucking whizzing that prime directive. She has NO qualms about this, it’s just bam, prime directive shattered. She fucking teleports in front of this guy.

“Are you a god?” “Yes” MICHAEL. DO YOU KNOW WHAT THE PRIME DIRECTIVE IS AND WHY IT EXISTS?

WHY ARE YOU A STARFLEET CAPTAIN.

Maybe eventually you won’t kill yourselves for no reason, idiots”.

Anyways they get the thing and go home whatever.

Erigah - DIS 1.5/10

The Federation captures Moll and L’ak and bring them into custody. Nhan is here again. Remember her? She’s uh, she’s here now again! Man they just write people out with tearful goodbyes then bring them back CONSTANTLY. If someone doesn’t fucking die, a goodbye means nothing.

Someone sent the “Eto, bleh~” gif from that one anime and it broke chat for a minute after this.

They’re not THAT far away, y’all, it’s been like 700 years.

When the Breen DO show up, they try to slow them down with legislation. It doesn’t really work, they have one hour to comply or it’ll be an act of war. That thing up there is the Breen ship btw. Remember when we saw the giant Romulan ship, the D’deridex for the first time and it dwarfs the Constitution? Or the Borg Cube and it’s even larger than that? Yeah uh, it’s getting old. Also I dunno why exactly the Breen have huge-ass ships like this. They sure didn’t in DS9.

We get some Tragic Backstory for Rayner. He hates the Breen because apparently they ruled over Kellerun for a while. A lot of this is giving me the energy of that one TNG episode with the Cardassians and O’Brien, but I know this won’t be NEARLY as good.

They try to bluff the Breen into accepting a deal with them. It almost works, but then it turns out the guards they set to watch L’ak are FUCKING BAD and he kills himself in his cell. The resulting battle between Moll and everyone is fucking painful to watch, it just sso much and the camera is FLAILING.

lmfao “IF ANY HARM FALLS TO L’AK BY THE FEDERATION, WAR IS INEVITABLE.” “We swear he will not be harmed.” “Hey uh, Burnham, it’s Laan, I have some news for you”. IT’S ALMOST COMEDIC.

I should still REALLY be liking Moll but I do not. She’s a rebel without a cause. She’s antagonistic because she refuses to not be, and she could EASILLY work with us instead.

Oh good, we’re making sure she’s COMPLETELY irradeemable! She sides with THE FUCKING BREEN and tells them about the super weapon and says she’ll tell them how to get to it. I mean, tbf, she wouldn’t actually be able to get to the weapon, she doesn’t fucking know where it is and is like 3 clues behind.

God I cannot care about this. I guess at least we’re not at war.

Labyrinths - DIS 2/10

We are so annoyed with having to watch this that we are now watching at 125% speed. These episodes feel like they are a million years long.

Anyways, Moll is now allied with the Breen and says she’ll use the Progenitor’s weapon to bring L’ak back to life. YOU DON’T EVEN REALLY KNOW WHAT THE PROGENITOR’S THING DOES, NO ONE HAS SEEN IT IN 800 YEARS.

Meanwhile, Discovery makes it to the Badlands, which is apparently where the next clue is kept. Remember the Badlands from DS9? This is the successor season for DS9! I hate my life!

They’re visiting a library that’s just sitting in the middle of the Badlands. They have to fly through the Badlands, which in DS9 was dangerous but here it just almost makes Discovery explode. They have a library card that allows them to like, check out this weapon or whatever. Dude, I dunno.

I used to be a library. I should like big science fiction star trek library. It’s a giant tower of books, I built a place like this in Dwarf Fortress once. The archivists show them to a chamber linked to the library card, which just… has a book sitting in it. It’s just been there forever.

“It’s fun to have a book visit the library for a change!” the archivist says to Booker. That’s cute. She gives him a cutting of the Kweijan world tree, which he almsot cries at.

Michael touches a thing in the book and is locked in her own mind in a test. Everyone else now has to sit there and watch her lay on the ground knocked out. “Oh by the way if you fail this mission you will die. Sorry.” Wh-why? Why would they build it like this? “The creator of this wants you to succeed” SURE DOESN’T SEEM LIKE IT.

The Breen can track discovery for some reason, so they now know where they are. The Library tells them to go the fuck away. This archive should have some dangerous guns on it tbh, they should be able to handle a Breen ship. But of course the Breen have to be super impossible to overcome.

Oh come on Michael. We don’t love you now.

“Me being too focused on my job is why I lost Book.” Um, no. You lost Book because he tried really hard to do genocide. I know, those two things are easy to mix up.

All her weird therapy session about her fears of death and her workaholic personality would be good, if it wasn’t all the correct thing for her to do at all points because she’s always been right always and is the perfect special boy. Anyways it turns out this is the correct thing, because “to handle what the progenitors left behind, you must be able to express your emotions like fear, guilt, and doubt”. SHE’S LITERALLY NEVER EXPRESSED THOSE IN ANY OTHER EPISODE OF THIS SERIES :D

Anyways they succeed in getting the thing and leave and the Breen just start attacking it. They demand that Michael hand over the map they got or they’ll destroy the archive. So Michael hands it over if they swear a blood oath, though she sets up a trick in case they blow her up to get away and pretend she’s been killed. They blow her up, and then decide to kill it anyways cause ha ha, they’re evil! Moll ends up just… killing the Breen leader instead. And all the Breen for some reason isntantly join under her banner.

I guess I liked the library in this one.

Lagrange Point - DIS 2/10

Hey, thats a fun Famicom game.

They gotta get to where the Precursor weapon is before the Breen do. Now that the previous Breen leader is dead lots of other Breen leaders are heading there to try and take his ship and soldiers under their banners. So now Discovery has to get there as soon as they can. They show up to two black holes and find a case floating in the lagrange point between them. Then the Breen instantly show up and just park right next to the black holes, because that ship is invincible until we need to blow it up later this season.

Moll nabs the progenitor’s box, and we need to steal that back, so Michael and gang sneak on board pretending to be Breen. This place is so fucking green. Waht is this, the Borg?

Michael has to do some fiddling while Book distracts a Breen guard. Book flirts with him. It’s actually a little funny. It took 5 seasons but we finally found banter that kind of works. Book just pulling out the Kris Special and flirting with someone he knows nothing about, and it somehow landing. “I will make a space for you in the oil bath” “Yo Michael hurry up this is getting weird”.

Saru has to go risk his life. He and his girlfriend hug. Hey, come on. Kira kissed Odo’s makeup-covered face and smeared it all over herself, go ham on this guy!

The sneaking plan fails so Discovery takes on this giant Breen ship and blows it up easily. ….Told you. Michael and Moll dive into the Precursor tech and disappear to who knows where.

Life, Itself - DIS 2/10

Here we are. The payoff. Everything we’ve ever worked towards is here at last. Also once again, important to note that all of this came about because they watched an okay episode of TNG and completely misunderstood the point of it.

Anyways Michael is in some weird dimension. She’s thrown around after touching some shit and lands in a rainy space. There are ALSO Breen in this space, and when they show up they just try to kill her for no reason. When Michael finally meets up with Moll, turns out the Breen are attacking her now too. Why? Wh-why???? She’s their leader last they knew. Moll and Michael team up.

Nevermind, Michael immediately turns on her and kicks her legs out. And then instead of stealing her gun, runs away????? We then get a VERY CGI fight scene.

Meanwhile on the Discovery, we get the conclusion to the Culber and Stamets storyline. Culber goes on a suicide mission so he can finish “trying to find what he’s looking for”, whatever that means. Culber and Stamets deserved better.

Michael and Moll team up…. AGAIN. “STAND DOWN, MOLL!” You’re the one that kicked her!!! Michael then solves the puzzle and techno babbles her way through the maze.

Moll betrays Michael this time. She listens to Michael to how to use the machine, then knocks her out and tries to revive her husband. She fails because she wasn’t listening and sets up the machine improperly. She has literally spent this entire season just ignoring everyone who’s trying to talk to her and help her. So, y’know, it fits. I do not like this character.

Saru comes back to be cool one last time and convince the Breen reinforcements to turn around and leave by having the best poker face. Well, at least Saru is still cool.

Michael wakes up, and fixes Moll’s stupid nonsense, solving the puzzle by herself and activating the mechanism properly. She then meets a Progenitor. I’d like to think the Progenitors are all women since we’re only met two. She’s like “Hi, I am a brain recording here to tell you how to operate this technology without killing anyone.”. She also says 2 things: 1) It can make a genetic clone but they have none of the personality of memories. We already have that, it’s called cloning. Then 2) The Progenitors did not actually make this technology, they just found it, and assume whoever made it made them. omfg.

If this wasn’t already a franchise with MULTIPLE godlike being established, this MIGHT be meaningful!

We get a 2001 Space Odyssey scene, with Michael deciding not to use the Life Device after seeing like, God or whatever. I honestly dunno. I don’t understand 2001, and that’s GOOD. Anyways, she goes back to Discovery, everything is calm and good now, and she’s like “We need to blow that thing up.” “But our orders are to bring it back for the Federation!” “Yeah well, they’ve always let me do whatever I want before with no reprucussions so this’ll be fine too.” “Makes sense to me.”

Moll is incarcerated, but Book is like “it should be fine, we can make sure you get a fair trial”. Ha ha, a LOT of people died because of her. Cronenberg is like “We’ll turn her into a secret agent it’s fine.”

SPEAKING of Cronenberg, we find out he’s under a codename. His real name is… Agent Daniels. YES. FOR REAL. THIS IS SO SLOPPILY REVEALED.

Saru gets married, which is cute. Still no kiss. Tilly decides she’s gonna start a mentorship program at Starfleet Acadamy. YOU DIDN’T HAVE ONE OF THOSE?! Aaaand Book and Michael get back together. Come on, he’s been doing SO MUCH BETTER after the whole genocide terrorism fiasco.

We then jump ahead into the future and see Old Michael. We then get a BIG extra long scene of Michael, Book, and their son. They live in a magical red forest with a magical deer neighbor. I love that deer tbh. And honestly I’d live in this house in a heartbeat. This is like, almost a magical christmas commercial… Finally, some real Raktajino.

Michael is an Admiral! We won’t see her get to that point, but she got there I guess. She and her son go and see The Discovery, which is being re-named “The Discovery A”. Why is this still going? She’s here to send the ship, and Zora, to the edge of space and have her sit there alone for as long as something will happen.

Why does this happen? So Calypso, the Short Trek episode, could happen. Yes. They really cared THIS HARD to make that accurate, and retconned it to make it happen in the 43rd century. So now to fix this they have Zora, completely sapient, just being sent to sit around for a thousand years for a reason they will never explain. We’ve already established that Zora is a life form. Why are we doing this? Also the future seen in Calypso is kinda dark and sucks. This blows.

Then we get scenes of the rest of the crew coming on board, and they’re all young again, so uh, it’s the end of the Titanic.

Off the Discovery goes, to the middle of nowhere. Goodbye. Maybe this is the fate it deserves.

….

……..

I hated this entire show and will never watch it again as long as I live. There was maybe one episode that’s a standout and that’s it. God damn.

entry.content:
The Wii rollout is now in full effect. I have to get like 50 something points in order to get a special event badge. 1 for a beat, 2 for a mastery, but some games are doubled. I won’t show all the games I played, because some of them I only beat. In fact…. Most of them! I beat 21 games for the Wii over the course of a few months, and only mastered 9 of them. Those beats are for more complicated games like Smash Bros, Animal Crossing, Monster Hunter, and Xeno Blade, though I got REALLY close to mastering Xenoblade I just got tired of grinding.
